session.question: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
session.answer:
The learning curve for DIEP flap breast reconstruction improved over time, but the pattern depended on whether outcomes were assessed at the institution or single-surgeon level. At the institutional level, the main change in later cases was a shorter hospital stay, while most other perioperative and complication outcomes remained similar between early and late periods. (varnava2023breastreconstructionwith chunk 1)

At the single-surgeon level, the improvement was more pronounced and reflected greater efficiency rather than lower complication rates. Total operative time decreased in later cases for both single and double DIEP flaps, and flap ischemia time also became shorter. However, flap loss and other complication rates did not differ significantly between early and late groups. (varnava2023breastreconstructionwith chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-c61287ea: The study examined a learning curve for DIEP flap breast reconstruction at both the institution and single-surgeon levels using early vs late cases. At the institution level, the main improvement over time was shorter hospital stay in late cases; otherwise, there were no significant differences between early and late periods. At the single-surgeon level, performance improved substantially with time: total surgery time decreased for both single and double DIEP cases, and flap ischemia time also shortened. Flap loss and other complication rates did not differ significantly between early and late groups, suggesting improved efficiency rather than fewer complications.
